report:
Reviewed the complete meta.reviews.review_delegation claim, its single ordinary implementation association (review.rs PROMPT), and its complete associated ordinary test, review_skill_assigns_one_owner_and_requires_start_read_record. Captured the checklist skill itself with review read, together with review specification and repository documentation. No TODO or not_applicable entries are present and no behavior is being approved as deferred.

This is a contract about instructions in the repository skill and the reviewer's workflow, not an assertion that Cargo automatically spawns agents or enforces agent identity. The checklist's coordinator section explicitly requires one subagent per failing anchor including TODO/N/A, passing its anchor ID and instructions to start and inspect printed inputs. It requires a single owner per validation directory, allows different anchors concurrently, and requires extra coordinator instructions through start --instructions while prohibiting uncaptured source context. The reviewer section directs additional context through read and completed reports through record; the follow-up section requires coordinator reconciliation, fresh delegated start/read/record reviews after changes, and cargo meta check. These clauses account for every qualification in the complete claim, including TODO/N/A and concurrent reviews. The implementation-associated PROMPT independently instructs the assigned subagent to inspect all claim and evidence aspects, capture extra dependencies, record its report, and restart after edits or stale input. The supplied whole review.rs supports that workflow with start's captured instructions and initial inventory, capture_read's appended fragments, and record's freshness check and saved output. Ownership is an agent workflow responsibility as specified, not a process-lock identity guarantee.

The annotated test includes the actual repository skill using include_str and visibly asserts one/subagent/anchor vocabulary, all three command spellings, instructions, and both TODO and N/A. These assertions detect removal of the workflow's command interface or its placeholder coverage; they do not prove agents obey prose, and they are not interpreted as such. Inspection of the captured actual skill establishes the exact assignment, ownership, parallelism, recorded-context, and coordinator follow-up meaning around those assertions. For this instructional contract, the content regression checks together with direct review of the complete instructions provide adequate evidence without asserting runtime scheduling behavior. No extra source helpers are used by this test.

Executed cargo meta review start meta.reviews.review_delegation with the supplied instructions file and cargo meta review read for additional source dependencies. Source assessment is independent of execution: I did not run a test suite or cargo build. Coordinator separately reports 321 passing functional sage-meta tests and a passing root cargo build; those are reported results, not commands executed by this reviewer. No production or test source changes were made. No concrete implementation discrepancy or missing prerequisite was found; no edits are requested.
